message.content:
This repository is a memo application (likely "Memos"). I need to find EVERY distinct server-side enforcement site where memo visibility (who may view a memo — PUBLIC, PROTECTED/WORKSPACE, PRIVATE) is checked/enforced.

Visibility levels are typically PUBLIC, PROTECTED (workspace/logged-in users), PRIVATE (creator only).

Search the server code (Go files, likely under server/, store/, api/ directories) for where visibility is enforced — anywhere the code decides whether a requesting user is allowed to view/access a memo based on its visibility field and the creator/current user.

There are at least three distinct enforcement sites. Look for:
- GetMemo / read single memo handler
- ListMemos / listing memos handler (filter building)
- Any RSS / streaming / attachment / resource / permalink surface that also enforces visibility
- Any shared helper function used to check visibility

For each enforcement site, report:
- A short name of the site (e.g. "GetMemo RPC handler", "ListMemos filter")
- The exact file path
- The line number(s) and a brief description of how visibility is enforced there

Be thorough — check every server surface. List all distinct sites with file paths.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
I have a complete picture of every server-side memo visibility enforcement site. Here is the full inventory.

## Core shared helper

**1. `checkMemoReadAccess` — the central single-memo visibility gate**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines **39-68**
- Logic: if memo is `Archived`, only the creator may read it (lines 44-53). Then if `Visibility != Public` (line 55), an authenticated user is required (60-62); if `Visibility == Private` and `CreatorID != user.ID`, permission denied (63-65). PROTECTED is allowed for any logged-in user.
- This is the shared helper reused by three callers:
  - `GetMemo` RPC handler at line **356** (and again at **367** for a comment's parent memo)
  - `ListMemoComments` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` line **148**

## Listing / filter-building enforcement sites (each builds its own visibility SQL/CEL filter)

**2. `ListMemos` filter**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines **218-227**
- Anonymous callers get `VisibilityList = [Public]`; a logged-in caller with no creator filter gets `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`; when listing another user's memos, restricted to `[Public, Protected]`.

**3. `ListMemoComments` filter**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, lines **156-160**
- Anonymous → `visibility == "PUBLIC"`; logged-in → `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC","PROTECTED"]`.

**4. `ListMemoRelations` filter (memo_relation_service.go)**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines **107-112**
- Same anonymous vs. logged-in filter pattern applied to related memos.

**5. Batch relation converter filter**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines **182-186** (in `batchConvertMemoRelations`)
- Same filter pattern; controls which related memos are exposed when converting memos to API responses.

**6. User stats filters**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go`, lines **87-90** and **220**
- Same `creator_id || visibility in [...]` filter and `VisibilityList = [Public, Protected]` restriction when aggregating stats for another user.

## RSS surfaces

**7. Explore RSS feed**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, line **90** (`GetExploreRSS`) — hard-restricts to `VisibilityList = [store.Public]`.

**8. User RSS feed**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`, line **141** (`GetUserRSS`) — same `[store.Public]` restriction.

## SSE / streaming surface

**9. SSE event delivery gate — `SSEClient.canReceive`**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`, lines **134-146**
- For `Private` events, only delivers to `userID == CreatorID` or admin; `Public`/`Protected`/empty are delivered to all connected clients.
- Related helper: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_event_helpers.go` (resolves a comment's parent CreatorID so private-comment events route correctly).

## Attachment / resource / file surfaces

**10. FileServer attachment permission — `checkAttachmentPermission`**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`, lines **650-704** (invoked at line 149 in `serveAttachmentFile`)
- Public + anonymous-allowed instance → allowed (677); share-token fallback for private/protected (684-689); otherwise requires auth (695-697); `Private` denied unless creator or admin (699-701).

**11. API attachment access (v1) — GetAttachmentBinary path**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, lines **445-451**
- Public → allowed; `Private` denied unless creator or super-user.

**12. Memo-attachment listing/access service**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`, lines **214-222**
- If memo `Visibility != Public` requires a user (214); `Private` denied unless creator or super-user (222).

## Reaction surface

**13. Reaction service visibility gate**
- File: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`, lines **30-38** (upsert) and line **83** (delete/list path)
- Non-public memos require a user; `Private` denied unless creator or super-user.

## Store layer (where the VisibilityList filter is actually applied to SQL)

**14. Store `VisibilityList` → SQL `WHERE visibility IN (...)`**
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, lines **96-102**
- Equivalent implementations: `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go` and `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go`
- This is the low-level enforcement that turns `FindMemo.VisibilityList` (set by sites #2, #6, #7, #8) into a SQL predicate. Visibility constants defined in `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` lines 16-31.

## Related non-read-gate uses (for completeness — these branch on visibility but govern notifications/mentions, not view access)

- Comment auto-visibility rule: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` lines 41, 100.
- Mention notification suppression for private memos: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` lines 62, 67, 84.
- Email notification gating on private/protected: `/bench/repo/server/notification/email.go` lines 313-316 and `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` lines 309-312.

### Bottom line — the distinct read-access enforcement sites
The primary/canonical ones the task asks about: **#1 `checkMemoReadAccess`** (shared helper backing GetMemo + comment reads), **#2 ListMemos filter**, and the additional surfaces **#7/#8 RSS**, **#9 SSE**, **#10-12 attachment/resource**, **#13 reactions**, plus the parallel filter builders **#3/#4/#5/#6**, all ultimately enforced at the SQL layer in **#14**.
